clue.text: Agreed to restore silver ball

indicators.note: to restore something is to rebuild it, so the given word is put back together in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone has consented to repair a decorative silver ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragee is the small silvered sugar sphere used for decorating cakes.

clue.text: See 16
Radar, for example, finds buddy in America

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: a crony is a close pal

explanation.surface: Someone called Radar meets a pal in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: Radar looks like a name or a gadget, but it stands for 'radio detection and ranging', so it is an ACRONYM.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar is a word formed from the initial letters of a longer phrase, which is exactly what an acronym is.

clue.text: Having the gift of the gab, the Spanish love to question English books

definitions.text: Having the gift of the gab

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, a round O
the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking Spaniard enjoys quizzing people about English literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with the gift of the gab speaks fluently and persuasively, which is what eloquent means.

clue.text: Traveller has company for short distance, but not time to speak

parts.note: millimetres, a very short distance, abbreviated

indicators.note: 'but not' excludes the following item, so it is struck out of the word for speak

explanation.surface: A traveller has companions on a brief trip but no chance to talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short distance' looks like the length of the journey, but it is a millimetre count, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: A commuter is someone who travels regularly between home and work.

clue.text: A grandparent, for example, may be intemperate

definitions.meaning: first meaning: spoil grandchildren with too many treats
second meaning: eat or drink to excess

explanation.surface: Doting grandparents may lack restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a sentence awaiting its verb: grandparents notoriously OVERINDULGE the children. The second sense is excess in food and drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both pampering someone too much and having too much yourself, which is being intemperate.

clue.text: Tree climbing? Have a go at climbing inside a shrub

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means read upwards, so the tree's letters run backwards
one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to have a go is to try, read upwards

explanation.surface: Someone shins up a tree and attempts to clamber into a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, and the clue uses it twice, once for each piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is an evergreen shrub with fragrant white flowers, sacred to Venus.

clue.text: A goodly number keep the Sabbath dry

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sabbath

explanation.surface: Many people observe a Sunday without drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep the Sabbath' reads as religious observance and 'dry' as teetotal, but dry here means wanting a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirsty and dry both describe someone in need of something to drink.

clue.text: Lad about to take exam again is impervious

indicators.note: one thing about another goes around it, wrapping it

parts.note: to sit an exam a second time

explanation.surface: A boy who must sit an exam again remains unmoved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning', but it tells the retake word to wrap around the lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impervious is unaffected by an influence, just as something resistant withstands it.

clue.text: Tom goes round right over the box

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
on, as in placed over or upon

explanation.surface: A tomcat circles and jumps over a box.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom is a male cat, not a person's name; it wraps around R, with ON after.
explanation.definitionFit: A carton is a light cardboard box or container.

clue.text: Some costermongers make a habit of taking first prize for potatoes

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Street traders routinely scoop the top award for their potatoes.
explanation.walkthrough: Pearly kings and queens are London costermongers (street fruit and vegetable sellers) whose clothes are covered in pearl buttons. Earlies are the first potatoes of the season.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearlies is the informal name for the pearly kings and queens, a tradition of London costermongers.

clue.text: River Test is out of the way for fat cats

indicators.note: turned out, so the abbreviation that follows is set the other way about

explanation.surface: Hampshire's River Test is out of bounds for wealthy anglers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River Test' looks like one name, the Test in Hampshire, but River gives INDUS and Test gives TRIAL. The final ST for street is turned to TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Fat cats is slang for rich business bosses, and industrialists are owners of manufacturing firms.

clue.text: Taking the blame, cutie-pie, may make you feel better

parts.note: taking the rap means taking the blame, so the blame is THE RAP

indicators.note: printer's pie is type that has been jumbled, so the word attached to it is mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Telling a sweetheart you'll shoulder the blame might cheer them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutie-pie' reads as a term of endearment, but 'pie' is the anagram signal, from printer's pie (jumbled type).
explanation.definitionFit: Something therapeutic has a healing or soothing effect, so it may lift your spirits or health.

clue.text: Girl missing last dance at end of autumn, which is becoming quieter

indicators.note: the dance and the season's letter are set at the girl's centre

parts.note: a girl's name, the Queen of Carthage

indicators.note: missing last means the final letter of the dance is dropped
end of asks for only the closing letter of the season

explanation.surface: A girl skips the final dance at the close of autumn as things grow quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl is Dido, Queen of Carthage, split open to take the shortened dance and the season's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Diminuendo is the musical term for a gradual decrease in loudness.

clue.text: Surprise, stupid! There's nothing in the kitty!

parts.note: dumb means stupid, especially in American use

indicators.note: something being in another means it sits inside it

parts.note: a kitty is a pooled fund of money

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked to find the shared money pot empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprise, stupid!' sounds like an insult, but Surprise is a verb definition and stupid gives DUMB.
explanation.definitionFit: To dumbfound someone is to astonish or amaze them so they are speechless.

clue.text: Bird distinguishable from many around

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are turned about into a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A single bird stands out from the many around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The myna is an Asian starling famous for mimicking human speech.

clue.text: Come a cropper in seasonal abode?

parts.note: the season, the American name for autumn

explanation.surface: Someone takes a tumble at home in autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: To come a cropper is British slang for to fail badly or take a heavy fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan or joke that fails to make its intended impression is said to come a cropper, i.e. to flop.

clue.text: Yard detective pursues rabble by the book

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow behind, so the yard-and-detective pair comes after the crowd

explanation.surface: A Scotland Yard detective chases a mob strictly by the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yard detective' suggests Scotland Yard, but Yard is just Y. 'Pursues' puts Y and the detective after MOB.
explanation.definitionFit: Herman Melville's novel about the white whale is a celebrated book, hence the definition.

clue.text: On the clergy's head be it; art is metamorphosed

definitions.note: describes where the answer is worn rather than naming it

indicators.note: metamorphosed means changed in form, so these letters take on a new shape

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: The responsibility rests with the clergy if art is transformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On your head be it' is an idiom about responsibility, but here it literally names headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is the square cap worn by Roman Catholic priests and other clergy.

clue.text: Progenitor protecting boy from legislators

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: a progenitor is a parent or ancestor

explanation.surface: A father shields his son from the lawmakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliament is the body of elected lawmakers, a collective of legislators.

clue.text: Make Sir be responsible for kick upstairs

definitions.meaning: first meaning: confer a title such as knighthood
second meaning: move a politician out of the way by elevating them to the House of Lords

explanation.surface: Someone who knights a person is behind their promotion away from power.
explanation.walkthrough: To kick someone upstairs is a British idiom for removing them from influence by promoting them, classically with a peerage.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble is to raise someone to the nobility or grant a title, the honour behind both phrases.

clue.text: King, temporarily lost for words, left after me to get a drink

parts.note: the hesitation noise of someone at a loss

explanation.surface: A tongue-tied king leaves after me to fetch a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left after me' places L after ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Kummel is a sweet colourless liqueur flavoured with caraway and cumin.

clue.text: Forthcoming seaside attraction?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as 'telling what is coming forth', predicting the future
second meaning: the clairvoyant's booth on a pier or promenade

explanation.walkthrough: Forthcoming seems to mean 'soon to arrive', describing the attraction; it is a separate, punning sense on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Predicting what lies ahead is the clairvoyant's trade, and palm-reading booths are a traditional feature of British resorts.

clue.text: A character on the staff

parts.note: setter's reading: a symbol placed on the musical stave

explanation.walkthrough: Staff suggests employees and character an odd person, but the staff is the five lines of music notation.
explanation.definitionFit: A clef is the sign at the start of a musical stave fixing the pitch of the notes.

clue.text: Last month I met defeat: this is the end

parts.note: ult., short for ultimo, means of last month in old business letters

explanation.surface: A disappointed player recalls being beaten last month: that was the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' wants to be the definition, but it pairs with month for ULT.
explanation.definitionFit: The ultimate is the final or furthest point, the last word in something.

clue.text: Universal high ball in endless high wind

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it
endless means the final letter of the wind is cut off

parts.note: a strong wind; loses its end
a ball hit high in the air

explanation.surface: A lofted shot is carried on a strong gust everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: GALE without its E becomes GAL, which holds LOB.
explanation.definitionFit: Something global applies to the whole world, so it is universal in reach.

clue.text: Hairstyle king and subject initially abandoned — nothing doing!

indicators.note: abandoned items are left behind, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: a style of matted, rope-like hair
R for rex, Latin for king; dropped

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of subject; dropped

explanation.surface: A king and his subject reject a hairstyle, refusing outright.
explanation.walkthrough: DREADLOCKS loses R and S to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock is a standstill where neither side will give way, so no progress happens.

clue.text: Is felt, perhaps, to be egocentric?

definitions.note: adjective clued; the answer is a reflexive pronoun

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters might be arranged some other way

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Is a feeling a sign of being self-centred?
explanation.walkthrough: A word turned in on itself is egocentric in a playful sense; the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: An egocentric thing is centred on its own self, and the reflexive pronoun points back to the thing alone.
